A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present iReduct, which is an algorithm for releasing differentially private data summaries that are accurate in the relative error sense. iReduct is based on the observation that the relative error of the noisy answers is a function of the scale of the true answer, and that this scale is known to the data owner. iReduct therefore uses a scale-dependent noise scale, which leads to superior data utility for queries with smaller answers.
we propose a novel approach to achieve differential privacy that minimizes the relative error of the query answers, and thus improves their utility.
iReduct is the first technique that achieves the same level of privacy while minimizing relative errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scale of noise added to a query answer should be inversely proportional to the size of the answer, so that the relative errors are minimized for all queries.
it is possible to achieve privacy with reduced relative error.
the relative error of a query can be much more informative than its absolute error.
